title: Decide whether a dataset release is promotable
description: Compare candidate datasets against explicit promotion policies. Apply one remediation and see which evidence gates change, which remain blocked, and how many examples survive.
notice: The scenarios are teaching fixtures. Production thresholds must be owned by domain, safety, privacy, and model-evaluation teams and versioned with the release.

releases.label: Balanced candidate
releases.detail: Broad coverage with a moderate duplicate tail and one weak critical slice.

releases.label: Synthetic-scale candidate
releases.detail: Strong aggregate lift, but weak lineage, duplication, and reviewer agreement.

releases.label: Expert-narrow candidate
releases.detail: Excellent evidence quality with insufficient language and long-tail coverage.

policies.label: Offline experiment
policies.detail: Allows exploratory evidence, but still blocks privacy incidents and severe quality failures.

policies.label: General production policy
policies.detail: Requires reproducible lineage and representative held-out evidence before promotion.

policies.label: High-consequence policy
policies.detail: Uses stricter lineage, agreement, safety, and critical-slice requirements.

remediations.label: No remediation
remediations.detail: Evaluate the candidate exactly as submitted.

remediations.label: Deduplicate and re-score
remediations.detail: Remove near-duplicate clusters, then recompute quality and evaluation evidence.

remediations.label: Targeted review and collection
remediations.detail: Audit lineage and add reviewed examples to the weakest critical slices.
